Container.Name: nexbooks
Container.Overview: Your e-books and audiobooks on your own server, to read and listen to in the browser. One container, SQLite, and your books stay plain files in your folders. The library is a shelf of spines, a shelf for each genre, with covers and a sortable list one switch away. One book holds all its editions: EPUB, AZW3 and MOBI of a book are one edition, and the e-book and the audiobook stand side by side, each with its own place. The reader opens EPUB, MOBI, AZW3 and PDF. The player plays an audiobook of many files as one, with chapters, speed and a sleep timer. Several people each have their own place, wish list and reading stack, and the operator sees neither progress nor history. Browse shelves by topic, best sellers and the gaps in your series, and every author has a page with all their works. With your own indexers and a download program nexbooks can fetch books: it judges every hit by author, title, volume, language and format, and files a book only if it is the one you wished. nexbooks comes with no indexers and no sources of books, and you are responsible for loading only content you may use. Kindle, OPDS, KOReader and Kobo (beta) connect as e-readers. A second factor is required from the start, passkeys are supported, and accounts come by invitation or through OpenID Connect (one-button setup for authentik). This is an early release: keep a backup and open an issue when something is wrong.
Container.Description: Your e-books and audiobooks on your own server: read and listen in the browser, one book with all its editions, and fetching through your own indexers. Open the WebUI and create the first account; it becomes the operator. It needs the setup code from the container log (click the nexbooks icon, then Logs), a new one at every start until nexbooks is set up. To choose the code yourself, set Setup Code below. Right after the password the account sets up its second factor. Then make a library of a folder at or below /books in Settings, Libraries. Books is mapped read-only at first, and nexbooks changes nothing in it. To file fetched books there, or to turn on tidying (renaming and moving by a scheme), set Books to read/write. To fetch books, map the folder where your download program puts finished jobs to /downloads; a path the program reports differently is mapped once in nexbooks. Put nexbooks behind a reverse proxy with TLS before you use it from anywhere but your own network, then set Public URL and Trusted Proxies. Passkeys and notices on a phone need https. All data lives under /data: the SQLite database, covers, secret.key, backups and logs. Keep it on a local disk, never on an SMB or NFS share, because SQLite locking is not reliable over network filesystems. A backup holds the database, settings, covers and photos but not the books, so those belong in the backup your server makes anyway. Set PUID and PGID to the user that should own the files and can read your books. 99 and 100 are the Unraid defaults and work out of the box.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port you reach nexbooks at. Container port: 8000

Config.Name: Data (Container Path: /data)
Config.Description: Holds the SQLite database with accounts and the search index, covers, the key secret.key, backups and logs. Keep it on a local disk, not on a network share.

Config.Name: Books (Container Path: /books)
Config.Description: Your e-books and audiobooks. In Settings, Libraries, make a library of a folder at or below /books. Read-only is enough to read and listen; set it to read/write to file fetched books here or to turn on tidying.

Config.Name: Downloads (Container Path: /downloads)
Config.Description: Optional, for fetching books: the folder where your download program (SABnzbd, qBittorrent ...) puts finished jobs. A path the program reports differently is mapped once in nexbooks.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id that should own the files in /data and can read your books. 99 is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id that should own the files in /data and can read your books. 100 is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: Time Zone
Config.Description: Time zone for timestamps in the log, for example Europe/Berlin. Leave blank for UTC. People's own time zones come from their browsers.

Config.Name: Setup Code
Config.Description: The code the first account needs to become the operator. Leave blank: nexbooks makes a new one at every start until it is set up and writes it to the container log.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: The address people use to reach nexbooks, for example https://books.example.com when it sits behind a reverse proxy. Used for invitation links and the return address of OpenID Connect. Leave blank to take the address of the request; the same can be set later in the settings.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxies
Config.Description: Addresses or networks of your reverse proxies, comma separated, for example 172.16.0.0/12. Only their X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto (the rightmost value) are believed, so only they can tell nexbooks that a request came in over https; without it every sign-in seems to come from the proxy and the brake against password guessing cannot tell people apart.

Config.Name: Container Port (host networking only)
Config.Description: Leave this empty unless you switched Network Type to Host. In bridge mode the WebUI Port above already does the job and setting this will break it, because the mapping still points at 8000. On host networking the port inside the container is the port on your server, so use this to move nexbooks off 8000 if something else is already there.

Config.Name: Secret Key
Config.Description: Protects the server-side secrets (the OpenID Connect client secret, the mail password, the keys of indexers and download programs). Leave blank: nexbooks creates one on first start and keeps it in /data/secret.key.

Config.Name: Secure Cookie
Config.Description: auto marks the session cookie Secure when the request arrived over https, also behind a proxy listed under Trusted Proxies that sends X-Forwarded-Proto. Use on only if a proxy terminates TLS and forwards plain http without that header, and never if nexbooks should also be reachable over http, or nobody can sign in. off never marks it.
